transcription.tex: This chapter develops addition and double-angle formulae, combines sine and cosine into one function, and uses these ideas to solve equations and model periodic motion.
\textbf{1. Addition formulae}\[\sin(a+b)=\sin a\cos b+\cos a\sin b\]
\textbf{3. Combining sine and cosine}\par Find the maximum of \(2\sin x+\cos x\) and where it occurs.
\textbf{4. Modelling}\par A tide can be modelled by \(x=R\sin(2\pi t/5+\alpha)\), where \(t\) is hours after midnight.

sourceMapping.method: Native text and LaTeX conversion; acceptance tracked separately

transcription.tex: Addition formulae handle sums and differences of angles.
\textbf{Do I need to memorise these?}\par They are in the formula booklet, but aim to memorise them, especially sine and cosine.

\textbf{How to remember}\par The first function on the right matches the left. Sine mixes sine and cosine; cosine keeps matching pairs. Sine keeps the sign, cosine changes it. Tangent keeps the sign on top and changes it underneath.\par The identities apply wherever both sides are defined.

transcription.tex: Why is \(\sin(A+B)\) not generally \(\sin A+\sin B\)? Give a counterexample.
Sine is a function, so it need not distribute over addition; similarly \((a+b)^2\) is not generally \(a^2+b^2\).

slides.title: Geometric Proof of the Sine Addition Formula

transcription.tex: Geometric proof (not required for the exam). Let \(OY=1\) make angle \(A+B\) with the horizontal, so \(XY=\sin(A+B)\).
1. Resolve the unit line along directions making angles \(A\) and \(A+\pi/2\) with the horizontal. The perpendicular components have lengths \(\cos B\) and \(\sin B\).
2. Their vertical components are \(\sin A\cos B\) and \(\cos A\sin B\).
3. Add the vertical lengths:\[\sin(A+B)=\sin A\cos B+\cos A\sin B.\]

sourceMapping.method: Native text and LaTeX conversion; acceptance tracked separately

transcription.tex: Use the sine addition formula to prove the formula for \(\sin(A-B)\).
\[\sin(A-B)=\sin(A+(-B))\]\[=\sin A\cos(-B)+\cos A\sin(-B)\]\[=\sin A\cos B-\cos A\sin B.\]
Prove the formula for \(\cos(A+B)\). Hint: use the complementary-angle relation.
\[\cos(A+B)=\sin((\pi/2-A)-B)\]\[=\sin(\pi/2-A)\cos B-\cos(\pi/2-A)\sin B\]\[=\cos A\cos B-\sin A\sin B.\]

sourceMapping.method: Native text and LaTeX conversion; acceptance tracked separately

transcription.tex: Edexcel C3 January 2012, Q8(a).\par Use the sine and cosine addition formulae to prove the tangent addition formula.

\[\tan(A+B)=\frac{\sin A\cos B+\cos A\sin B}{\cos A\cos B-\sin A\sin B}.\]\par Divide every numerator and denominator term by \(\cos A\cos B\):\[=\frac{\frac{\sin A\cos B}{\cos A\cos B}+\frac{\cos A\sin B}{\cos A\cos B}}{1-\frac{\sin A\sin B}{\cos A\cos B}}=\frac{\tan A+\tan B}{1-\tan A\tan B}.\]\par Work where both sides are defined.

transcription.tex: Given \(2\sin(x+y)=3\cos(x-y)\), express \(\tan x\) in terms of \(\tan y\).

\[2\sin x\cos y+2\cos x\sin y=3\cos x\cos y+3\sin x\sin y.\]\par Where \(\cos x\cos y\ne0\), divide through:\[2\tan x+2\tan y=3+3\tan x\tan y.\]\[\tan x(2-3\tan y)=3-2\tan y\]\[\tan x=\frac{3-2\tan y}{2-3\tan y}.\]

sourceMapping.method: Native text and LaTeX conversion; acceptance tracked separately

transcription.tex: 2. Use the sine and cosine subtraction formulae to prove the tangent subtraction formula.
\[\tan(A-B)=\frac{\sin A\cos B-\cos A\sin B}{\cos A\cos B+\sin A\sin B}\]\par Divide each term by \(\cos A\cos B\), where defined:\[=\frac{\tan A-\tan B}{1+\tan A\tan B}.\]
3. Substitute \(A=P,B=-Q\) into the sine addition formula to obtain \(\sin(P-Q)\).
\[\sin(P-Q)=\sin P\cos(-Q)+\cos P\sin(-Q)\]\[=\sin P\cos Q-\cos P\sin Q.\]

transcription.tex: 11. Given \(\cos y=\sin(x+y)\), show that \(\tan y=\sec x-\tan x\).

transcription.tex: 16. Prove \(\cos\theta+\cos(\theta+2\pi/3)+\cos(\theta+4\pi/3)=0\). Show every stage of working.

Put \(\phi=\theta+2\pi/3\). Then\[\cos(\phi-2\pi/3)=\cos\phi\cos(2\pi/3)+\sin\phi\sin(2\pi/3),\]\[\cos(\phi+2\pi/3)=\cos\phi\cos(2\pi/3)-\sin\phi\sin(2\pi/3).\]\par Adding these and \(\cos\phi\), the sine terms cancel:\[2\cos\phi\cos(2\pi/3)+\cos\phi=2\cos\phi(-1/2)+\cos\phi=0.\]

transcription.tex: STEP I 2010 Q3.\par a. Show\[\sin(x+y)-\sin(x-y)=2\cos x\sin y.\]\par Hence show\[\sin A-\sin B=2\cos\frac{A+B}{2}\sin\frac{A-B}{2}.\]
\[\sin(x+y)-\sin(x-y)\]\[=\sin x\cos y+\cos x\sin y-(\sin x\cos y-\cos x\sin y)\]\[=2\cos x\sin y.\]\par Put \(x=(A+B)/2,y=(A-B)/2\) to obtain the required difference of sines.
\[\cos(x+y)-\cos(x-y)\]\[=\cos x\cos y-\sin x\sin y-(\cos x\cos y+\sin x\sin y)\]\[=-2\sin x\sin y.\]\par Use the same substitutions for \(x,y\).

c. Points \(P,Q,R,S\) have coordinates \((a\cos u,b\sin u)\) at \(u=p,q,r,s\), with \(a,b>0\) and \(0\le p<q<r<s<2\pi\). Assuming \(PQ,SR\) are not vertical, prove they are parallel exactly when \(r+s-p-q=2\pi\).

\[m_{PQ}=\frac{b(\sin q-\sin p)}{a(\cos q-\cos p)}\]\[=\frac{2b\cos((p+q)/2)\sin((q-p)/2)}{-2a\sin((p+q)/2)\sin((q-p)/2)}\]\[=-\frac ba\cot\frac{p+q}{2}.\]\par Similarly \(m_{SR}=-(b/a)\cot((r+s)/2)\). Equal slopes occur iff \((r+s-p-q)/2=k\pi\). Since \(0<r+s-p-q<4\pi\), only \(k=1\) is possible: the difference is \(2\pi\). Conversely this difference gives equal slopes.

transcription.tex: 6a. Write \(65\cos\theta-20\sin\theta=R\cos(\theta+\alpha)\), \(R>0,0<\alpha<\pi/2\), with \(\alpha\) to 4 d.p.\par A tourist height on a large wheel is \(H=70-65\cos0.2t+20\sin0.2t\), metres; \(t\) is minutes after boarding, angles in radians.
b. Find the maximum height.\par c. Find the time for one revolution.\par d. Find the time spent above 100 m per revolution.

\[H>100\iff\cos(0.2t+\alpha)<-30/R.\]\par Let \(\beta=\arccos(-30/R)\). The interval above 100 m in one cycle has angular length \(2\pi-2\beta\).\[\text{Duration}=\frac{2\pi-2\beta}{0.2}=11.1\text{ minutes (1 d.p.)}.\]\par The first crossing times are about 8.646 and 19.785 minutes.
